# Router experiment results (generated by `python -m ml.train`)

Data: 304 train / 51 val / 50 template-held-out test / 64 hand-written natural test. **Synthetic data**; treat absolute numbers as optimistic.

| model | test macro-F1 | natural-test macro-F1 | natural-test accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| rules baseline | 0.4692 | 0.3041 | 0.2969 |
| scikit-learn (TF-IDF+LR) | 0.4118 | 0.7097 | 0.7344 |
| PyTorch (mean±std, 5 seeds) | 0.4043±0.0827 | 0.4912±0.0137 | - |

Grouped 5-fold CV macro-F1: rules 0.4187±0.1301, sklearn 0.9057±0.0729.

## Largest confusions on natural test (scikit-learn)
- general_question → coding_assistance: 3
- general_question → memory_retrieval: 2
- general_question → research: 1
- general_question → data_analysis: 1
- research → voice_command: 1
- coding_assistance → research: 1

| 0.6 | 0.0 | None |

Chosen threshold **0.2**. Hybrid policy (model if confident else rules) on natural test: macro-F1 0.7704, accuracy 0.75, model used for 72% of requests.

> Caveat: the template-held-out `test` split has only 2 held-out templates per class, so its effective sample is ~16 templates and its F1 is very noisy (errors come in clusters). Grouped CV and the natural set are the more informative numbers. Tiny samples; no significance testing was done.

**Decision input:** natural-test macro-F1 {'rules': 0.3041, 'sklearn': 0.7097, 'torch': 0.4912, 'hybrid': 0.7704}; best = `hybrid`; best model beats rules by 0.4663.
